system.summary: Saxon system S1 of Wackerbarth's letters of 1715 and of his Vienna mission (March-June 1717), one key: homophonic substitution of French letters in 1-2 digit numbers (e 2/10, i 9, o 16/22/33, t 28/52 ...), polygrams and a nomenclator in 3-digit numbers (154 Votre Excellence, 177 le Czar, 187 le roi de Suède, 217 le roi d'Angleterre, 252 le roi de Prusse, 292 la Pologne, 306 Vienne, 355 premier), 4-digit numbers taken for nulls, clear words interspersed.
system.notes: One key in both volumes: key c (glosses of Loc. 00713/01) and K1715 (glosses of Loc. 00712/05) agree on 43 of their 47 common numbers by the verifier's comparison (the contributor counted 47 of 50), share 150, 168 and 700, and each reads the other volume's letter (verification, 12 Nov 2026). The four that differ: 20 (ee / b; b is right), 71 (y / i; the training glosses have y in all 8 cases, so s15_key.tsv's 'i' is a slip), 77 (ss / s), 97 (m / la). Key c's 103 = 'les' reads 'le' in Relation XXII ('le comte de Sinzendorf'). S1 is not the Flemming key K0 (Loc. 00675/10, view 0080), nor its shifted variant, nor Wackerbarth's 1703 key (contributor's comparison). The volume's Nov.-Dec. 1717 letters use another key (S2 = K0); they are outside this entry. By the contributor's report of A.-S. Rous's paper (not opened here), she describes the 1717 system as substitution in 1-3 digit numbers, mostly 2, with 355 and 1000 in the nomenclator.

prior_solution.where: Many S1 passages of both volumes carry interlinear decipherments of the time (the keys were rebuilt from them); the letter of 24 April 1717 has a decipherment sheet of the time (ff. 33-33v). Relation XXII and the letter of 20 Nov. 1715 have none (a few marginal words on the latter). A.-S. Rous (The Keys of Diplomacy, HistoCrypt 2024, University of Tartu repository) works on this correspondence; by the contributor's report of her paper she lists the 1717 letter as not deciphered. The paper could not be opened at integration (12 Nov 2026; abstract only), so this is not checked. An original key may survive: DECODE holds the Saxon key series of Loc. 03233/02 (not tried on S1), and a search snippet of Rous's 2022 book mentions Wackerbarth-Flemming nomenclators for the 1717 Vienna trip (book not opened).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocols hashed before each single measurement; a partial reading may be published if explained); on 11 Nov 2026, after the second measurement, he decided to accept the held-out language test alone as the condition for reading Relation XXII (post hoc, declared). Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, built the key, wrote and ran the protocols, read and wrote up. No human read the reading against the scans. For the letter of 20 Nov. 1715 he answered once a blind plate of digit shapes (W1, two controls passed) and approved adding the letter to this target.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, key, protocols, measurements, reading, write-up)

solution.what: Glossed S1 views (training) and their glosses, Relation XXII views 0089-0099 and the letter of 24 April 1717 (views 0037-0040) transcribed, each part hashed before decoding; the decipherment sheet of the time 0042-0043 transcribed.

Key rebuilt by aligning cipher groups on the interlinear decipherments of the time of the glossed S1 views 0017, 0057-0062, 0071-0072, 0080-0081, 0086-0088 (keys KEY-W1717, then b and c by a mechanical rule written beforehand). The sheet of 24 April was not a source of the key: it served only test A (view 0040) and a non-blind check.

Protocol 1 (hashed): test A (view 0040 vs the sheet of the time) 0.204 vs 0.086 for 200 permuted keys, under threshold; test B (lexical cover, 360 groups of Rel. XXII) 0.9375 vs 0.9231. Both failed; instrument at fault (diagnosed afterwards).

Protocol 2 (hashed), test A' (ground truth): the letter of 28 May 1717, glossed at the time, held out of key b; score = gloss words recovered exactly. Declared bar: at least 0.60 and a margin of at least 0.30 over the best of 200 permuted keys. Result 0.339 (195 words, 709 groups) against 0.128, margin 0.21: FAILED.

Protocol 2 (hashed), test B' (held-out language test): view 0091 of Relation XXII (353 groups, never decoded), key c, criterion L7 calibrated on the training views only (the list of candidate criteria had been widened after a first calibration failed, before the measurement): z = 11.5, gap 0.74 against 200 permuted keys: passed. The protocol allowed a reading only if A' and B' both passed, so under its own rule there was no reading.

Avenant 3, a rule changed after the result: Brice Dudout accepted B' alone as the condition for reading Relation XXII, with the 95% bar as the final check. By the contributor's record it was hashed before the remaining views were transcribed or decoded.

Relation XXII read by sense with frozen key c: 716 cipher words, by the contributor's marks 575 certain, 66 probable, 66 restored, 9 unresolved (641 = 89.5% by the contributor's count; see the integration recount for the figure under one rule). Letter of 24 April decoded against its sheet of the time (not blind): 188 of 207 by the same marks.

Letter of 20 Nov. 1715: key K1715 learnt only from the glossed views 0388-0390 of Loc. 00712/05 (majority vote, 57 numbers, 934 pairs), frozen before the measurement; same system as S1 of 1717 (47/50 common numbers agree).

Pre-registered single measurement (PREREG-1715) on the blind control portion view 0384 left (307 groups): S = 0.945 vs max of 400 witness keys 0.730, rank 1/401, threshold 0.77 calibrated on training only: passed.

Letter of 20 Nov. 1715 read by sense with K1715, completed by S1/1717 values and by values deduced in the letter; blind plate W1 of nine digit shapes answered by Brice Dudout (controls 2/2), three words corrected: 922 cipher words, by the contributor's marks 774 certain, 118 probable, 12 restored, 18 unresolved (892 = 96.75% by the contributor's count, which counts words resting on values deduced in the letter; see the integration recount).

Independent verification at integration (PR #418): frozen hashes match (PROTOCOLE.md excepted, as declared); keys b and c rebuild byte for byte from the glossed views; K1715 rebuilds from the training glosses (57 numbers, 934 pairs; one value differs, 71 = y not i); a second decoder gives the same Relation XXII; view 0091 with an own scorer and the project's French model: z = 7.3, above all 200 permuted keys; control page 0384 left: z = 5.7. Cross-volume check, not in the PR: K1715, learnt only from the 1715 glosses, turns Relation XXII into French (90% coverage, z = 8.8 over all 2,939 groups), and key c does the same for the 1715 letter (z = 5.6); K1715's glosses confirm 4 = x, 76 = st, 20 = b and give 306 = Vienne. Test A' could not be re-run (lexicon and corpora not in the PR).

Recount under one rule for the whole target (integration_recount.py: every word aligned on the numbers under it; a word counts only if the contributor read it and every number under it has a value in a key built from glosses of the time, key c or K1715, or a value a gloss attests: 4 = x, 76 = st, 20 = b, 306 = Vienne from the 1715 glosses, 78 = le from view 0057). Relation XXII 664 of 716 = 92.7%; letter of 20 Nov. 1715 841 of 922 = 91.2%; both under 95%, both read in part. Key check of 24 April (views 0037-0039): 193 of 207 = 93.2%.

A.-S. Rous, The Keys of Diplomacy (HistoCrypt 2024; DOI 10.58009/aere-perennius0111): the DOI, the Tartu repository item and its PDF, and the Wayback copy were all tried and refused from this network; only the title and abstract were read (OpenAlex record). What the paper says about these volumes stays the contributor's report, not checked. Record pages of both volumes read on archiv.sachsen.de (titles: Flemming-Wackerbarth correspondence, Bd. 291, 1717, and Bd. 288, 1715). DECODE keys of Loc. 03233/02 and Rous's 2022 book not opened.

Claims review by a second reader: the page's rule (every number under a counted word has a gloss value) was looser in integration_recount.py, which dropped a word only for a number with no value. Script made strict: a word counts only if the contributor read it and every letter of it as read is given by the gloss value of the number under it (key c, K1715, or a value a gloss attests: 4 = x, 76 = st, 20 = b, 306 = Vienne from the 1715 glosses, 78 = le from view 0057, 103 = le from view 0080); spelling equivalences u/v, i/j/y, single/double consonant, est/ét, à + le roy = au Roy only; a gloss-valued number read as other letters, passed over inside the word, or a letter with no number under it now drops the word; catchword of view 0384 left no longer counted, the 1715 letter aligned as one stream, clear words inside cipher lines given by the manuscript. Hand-checked on more than twenty words of each class against the transcriptions and decryption files. Relation XXII 664 -> 634 of 716 (92.7% -> 88.5%); 1715 letter 841 -> 741 of 922 (91.2% -> 80.4%); both 1,505 -> 1,375 of 1,638 (91.9% -> 83.9%); 24 April key check 193 -> 180 of 207 (93.2% -> 87.0%). 103 = le kept: a gloss of the time gives it (view 0080 L03, 'deloger les russes', 103 29 = les).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the interlinear glosses of the time on other letters in the same key: key c from views 0017, 0057-0062, 0071-0072, 0080-0081 and 0086-0088 of Loc. 00713/01, K1715 from views 0388-0390 of Loc. 00712/05. It was then applied to Relation XXII and to the letter of 20 Nov. 1715, which have no decipherment. The sheet of 24 April 1717 was not a source of the key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: integration_recount.py over reading files and frozen transcriptions, cipher words of the two letters read with the rebuilt key: Relation XXII 634 of 716 (88.5%) + letter of 20 Nov. 1715 741 of 922 (80.4%) = 1,375 of 1,638 = 83.9%. Strict rule after the claims review of 12 Nov 2026: a word counts only if the contributor read it and every letter of it as read is given by the gloss value of the number under it (key c, K1715, or a value a gloss attests: 4 = x, 76 = st, 20 = b, 306 = Vienne from the 1715 glosses, 78 = le from view 0057, 103 = le from view 0080); spelling equivalences u/v, i/j/y, single/double consonant, est/ét, à + le roy = au Roy only. Before the review the script dropped a word only when a number under it had no gloss value (664, 841, 1,505 = 91.9%). The contributor's own counts, under two different rules, were 89.5% and 96.75%.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered tests, not docs/_validate.py. The declared ground-truth test A' FAILED: 0.339 of gloss words exact on the held-out letter of 28 May 1717 against 0.128 for the best of 200 permuted keys, margin 0.21 where 0.30 and a score of 0.60 were required. The protocol required A' and the language test B' both; B' passed (view 0091, z = 11.5). Reading on B' alone is a rule changed after the result (Avenant 3). A first protocol (tests A and B) had also failed. Hence 'weak', not 'pass'. Other evidence, separate from the failed test: the 1715 letter's own pre-registered measurement passed (S 0.945 against 0.730, rank 1 of 401); and, checked at verification on 12 Nov 2026, each volume's key reads the other volume's letter (K1715 on Relation XXII: z = 8.8 over 2,939 groups; key c on the 1715 letter: z = 5.6), and every permuted-key control is beaten on every document with either key. Order of events by the contributor's record (all commits and timestamps are of 11 Nov 2026).

texts.label: Relation XXII, Wackerbarth to Augustus II, Vienna 14-16 June 1717
texts.summary: Chancellor Sinzendorf, by order of Charles VI, proposes to Wackerbarth (and the day before to Saint-Saphorin) a concert of the Emperor, the King of Poland and the King of England to restore the tranquillity of the Empire and an entire peace in the North on a just balance; Saint-Saphorin, as Wackerbarth reports it ('Selon lui'), thinks it might go as far as a triple alliance (his opinion, not Sinzendorf's proposal); the stay of the Russians in the Empire is referred to the Diet of Ratisbon and the directors of the Circles; George I wants the same measures regarding Poland and nothing returned to the King of Sweden; strict secrecy.

reading_review.note: reading.md read through as French against translation.md: coherent diplomatic prose from the first cipher word to the dating, the translation follows it; 'triple alliance' is Saint-Saphorin's opinion as the summary says. Raw: 82 words not counted under the strict rule (52 under the looser rule this review saw), three numbers probably misread. Not compared with the images beyond the verifier's sample (view 0091 left). The contributor's own review, also B, was by an AI agent.

texts.note: 634 of 716 cipher words counted under the target's one strict rule (integration_recount.py); the contributor's own count is 641 = 89.5%, which leaves out the 24 restored or unresolved words whose only missing value (4 = x, 76 = st, 20 = b, 306 = Vienne) the 1715 glosses supply, and counts 31 words the strict rule does not: 'le Czar' at a number probably misread, 'de' at 0094 D17, and 29 words where the reading gives a gloss-valued number other letters, passes one over or supplies a letter (garantir on 'xarentir', se on 78, donner on 'donqer', du from 'd' alone ...).

texts.label: Wackerbarth to Flemming, Vienna 24 April 1717 (read from the decipherment of the time)
texts.summary: The King of Sweden's designs on Poland (a landing near Danzig); the fear that Sweden may detach the Czar from the Northern League, which Vienna should thwart; the Hanau exchange: the Electors' consents must be won directly, not through the Emperor (promise of Ferdinand II to John George I); request for full power and a draft treaty.

reading_review.note: The sheet of the time as transcribed (frozen/releves/A-FEUILLE-0042-0043.txt) reads as continuous French and a24_translation.md follows it; the key-based reading of views 0037-0039 agrees with it in sense. Sheet transcription not compared with the image (view 0042 downloaded by the verifier, not compared).

texts.note: The text is the decipherment sheet of the time (399 words as transcribed, one doubtful: 'em:barasser'), shown as the reading and translated in a24_translation.md. a24_decryption.txt and a24_reading.md are the check with the rebuilt key on views 0037-0039: 180 of 207 cipher words under the target's one strict rule (188 by the contributor's count), not blind.

texts.label: Wackerbarth (camp before Stralsund) to his wife in Vienna, 20 November 1715, copy
texts.summary: Answering a 'reasoning' put to the countess at the imperial court, Wackerbarth says that Charles XII will be driven from the Empire (Stralsund closely besieged, Wismar blockaded since Poel was taken); Augustus II wants a general peace, not a separate one, and no total ruin of Sweden; the remnants that might carry Charles XII back to Poland should be destroyed now; he will write to General Dücker and ask Count Virmond to come, so that peace may be made under the Emperor's mediation.

reading_review.note: s15_reading.md read through as French against s15_translation.md: the cipher words construe with the clear text around them and the translation follows; the argument holds from page to page. Raw: page-by-page fiche with marks, 18 unresolved words, 53 words on deduced values and 98 on misread, skipped or supplied letters (strict rule; 51 and none under the looser rule this review saw). Not compared with the images beyond the verifier's sample (view 0384 left). The contributor's own review, also B, was by an AI agent.

texts.note: 741 of 922 cipher words counted under the target's one strict rule (integration_recount.py); the contributor's own count, 892 = 96.75%, also counts 53 words that rest on values deduced in this letter and 98 where the reading gives a gloss-valued number other letters, passes one over or supplies letters with no number under them (36 of these are words whose cipher stops short of the end, possibly the clerk's abbreviations; counting them would give 84.3%, a sensitivity figure only). The file names inside frozen/ keep the first, wrong date (1715-10-20).

outcome.notes: Contributed by Brice Dudout (PR #418), verified and integrated on 12 Nov 2026. One key in two volumes; the class and every count follow one rule (integration_recount.py). key.tsv section A = frozen key c; section B = proposals made after the measurement. s15_key.tsv = K1715 as frozen (its 71 = i should read y). The Nov.-Dec. 1717 letters of Loc. 00713/01 are in another key (the Flemming key K0) and are not part of this entry. No image of the Dresden scans is included: the archive's imprint reserves copyright on its images and the contributor reports the scans marked In Copyright. To be cited as simultaneous work with A.-S. Rous.
